validity.recommendation: Human review against SNGPL's own asset history before further edits. GEM's Dhulian->Daud Khel route (85.2 km, 8in) does not match either of the two real, differently-named/specced SNGPL systems that actually run through this corridor per SNGPL's own 2025 Annual Report: (1) 'Dhulian-Rawalpindi-Wah System' (82 miles / ~132km of 6-inch pipe, acquired from Attock Oil Company Ltd at SNGPL's 1963 inception) -- runs FROM Dhulian but TO Rawalpindi/Wah, not Daud Khel; (2) a separate '18" DIA x 130 KM FROM KAKA KHEL TO DAUD KHEL' transmission pipeline (a later, 1989-98-era project) -- runs TO Daud Khel but FROM Kaka Khel (Khyber Pakhtunkhwa), not Dhulian. GEM's P4164 appears to combine the Dhulian endpoint of system (1) with the Daud Khel endpoint of system (2) into a composite name/route that the owner's own history does not recognize as a single pipeline, with a third set of specs (85.2km/8in) that matches neither real system. Two explanations are plausible: a bulk-load conflation/mislabeling error, or GEM is simply missing the real 'Kaka Khel-Daud Khel' pipeline as its own entity (it does not appear anywhere in the 63-row Pakistan-gas roster) while P4164 stands in for it under the wrong name and specs. Recommend: (a) do not treat P4164 as independently verified as recorded; (b) check whether the real Kaka Khel-Daud Khel line (18in x 130km) should be added to GEM as a separate, missing pipeline (discovery candidate); (c) consider whether P4164 should be renamed/re-routed to genuinely match Dhulian-Rawalpindi-Wah (82mi/6in) if that is what it is meant to represent, or retired/merged if it is a pure artifact.
validity.researcher_notes: wiki_citations.json returned HTTP 403 for this row (Cloudflare-blocked harvest, confirmed empty per scope note) and my own WebFetch of the gem.wiki page also 403'd, so there was no existing sheet-cited source to re-verify -- this row's [ref] cells are all MISSING_REF per the worklist, consistent with the scope note that the whole batch came back with zero refs. I went straight to open-web/primary-source research. This session's WebSearch tool budget was exhausted (200/200 used by other concurrent subagents) before I started, and DuckDuckGo HTML search began returning CAPTCHA challenges partway through, so I worked mainly through targeted WebFetch of DuckDuckGo/Bing result pages (several of which returned garbled/mismatched cached content -- e.g. Bing returning firearms or German-grammar results for pipeline queries, a sign of cache pollution from the many parallel researcher sessions hitting the fetch service this run) plus direct WebFetch of primary-source PDFs once I had candidate URLs. No source anywhere used the exact phrase 'Dhulian-Daud Khel' for a pipeline. Two verified, independent, en-language news sources (energyupdate.com.pk, 2025-09-22 and 2026-01-08) DO confirm Daud Khel (Mianwali Dist., Punjab) is a real gas-consuming industrial site -- Agritech's Daud Khel fertilizer unit, allocated 50 MMCFD indigenous gas from the Mari field's Ghazij/Shawal reservoir via the government's fertiliser-sector gas allocation program -- so the END point of this row is a genuine, actively gas-supplied location, just not necessarily reached via a 'Dhulian' pipeline as named. Critically, I then downloaded SNGPL's own 2025 Annual Report (the pipeline's stated 100% owner) directly from sngpl.com.pk and ran pdftotext -layout on the full 14MB PDF (url_verifier's automated substring screen FAILed on this URL, but its own docstring documents this exact large-PDF false-negative class -- 'the extractor does not reach the whole document' -- and instructs downloading + pdftotext to confirm manually, which I did: both 'Dhulian' hits are verbatim and load-bearing, not noise). The report states verbatim (Corporate Profile, p.5): 'At inception, the Company acquired the existing Sui-Multan system... and the Dhulian-Rawalpindi-Wah System (82 miles of 6-inch diameter pipeline) from Attock Oil Company Limited,' and separately, in its Milestones timeline (p.75, 1989-98 entry): '18" DIA X 130 KM FROM KAKA KHEL TO DAUD KHEL... FOR INJECTION OF NEWLY DISCOVERED GAS FROM SHEWA WELL 1.' I searched the full report text for every mention of Dhulian, Daud Khel, Kaka Khel, Khaur, Toot, Meyal, and Potwar; these are the only hits, and 'Dhulian' and 'Daud Khel' never co-occur. A secondary, non-citable lead (PEPL's 2020 Energy Map PDF, pepl.com.pk -- fails url_verifier on an SSL certificate-chain error so it cannot be used as a ref) shows map labels 'DHULIAN' and 'DAUD KHEL' near a '10/12" GAS PIPELINE' label in the same general Attock/Mianwali corridor, which is at least suggestive that some pipeline runs through this area, but (a) I could not verify the map actually links these two specific named points as one pipeline versus adjacent-but-separate field/route labels, (b) I cannot cite it, and (c) its 10/12in label does not match GEM's stated 8in diameter either. Roster cross-check: no duplicate PID in the 63-row Pakistan-gas roster carries matching specs (85.2km/8in) or represents the real Kaka Khel-Daud Khel line -- that real line, if it exists as GEM should record it, appears to be entirely missing from the tracker. P4163 (Dakhni-Meyal-Dhulian, ending at Dhulian) is a plausible, non-duplicative upstream neighbor of P4164's stated start point, so the Dhulian end of this row is at least geographically coherent with the rest of the local roster even though the Daud Khel end is not corroborated as connected to it.

summary: P4164 flagged verdict=concern / concern_type=existence: SNGPL's own 2025 Annual Report documents a real 'Dhulian-Rawalpindi-Wah' system (82mi/6in, ex-Attock Oil Co.) and a separate real 'Kaka Khel-Daud Khel' pipeline (18in x130km), but neither matches GEM's Dhulian->Daud Khel/85.2km/8in route -- likely a conflation or a stand-in for a missing real entity; no fills staged given the identity/route doubt.
